content.comment_body: Hello, I'm working on a project involving a [product_name] with [version_no], including three expansion modules, which together should provide 20 digital outputs and 24 digital inputs. While programming in [product_name] Soft Comfort, I can easily access all 24 digital inputs, but only 16 digital outputs are available. Is there a maximum limit of 16 outputs in the software, or could I be missing something? When trying to assign outputs to the power bus, options for outputs 17-20 are unavailable in the dropdown.
Hi, I'm not an expert but from what I know, if you need more outputs, you might need to add another [product_name] and set it as a slave. It's best to wait for further expert advice.
You don't need expert help for this—just refer to the manual. The manual can be found at [url]. If you need additional outputs, you'll need another [product_name] ([article_no]).

If you need more than 16 outputs, you should upgrade your [product_name] from [article_no] to [article_no], and use at least two devices to reach up to 32 outputs. For more than 32 outputs, add more devices as needed. Note that only up to eight [article_no] units can be networked together, allowing a total of 128 outputs.
You can find the manual at [url]. To extend outputs, you will need additional [product_name] ([article_no]).

analysis.insight_summary: The user experienced a limit in the programmable number of digital outputs, accessing only 16 where the hardware should support more. Community responses clarified that both the software and hardware for [product_name] with [version_no] restrict outputs to 16, suggesting upgrading hardware or adding more units to increase output capacity. Reference materials such as the manual were shared for further details, and some users were uncertain whether the limitation was software- or hardware-based, relying on forum support for clarification.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects to use all digital outputs provided by the base and expansion modules without encountering further hardware or software restrictions, and seeks to understand whether the limitation is software-related or a result of incorrect setup.
